# Which side would the three people on the bridge have come from?

## Short answer

They would have come from the **right-hand side of the picture** — the near, right-hand bank where the red torii gate stands and the cliff-side path runs. They are walking away from that bank and out across the bridge toward the **left-hand bank**.

(All "left" and "right" below are from the viewer's point of view, as we look at the print.)

## The three figures

The group on the plank bridge is, from left to right: a small child in a red patterned kimono, an adult in a dark striped kimono, and a woman in a pale white kimono who carries a red cloth bundle (furoshiki) and a closed umbrella/parasol tucked under her arm.

## Why the answer is "from the right"

**1. The bridge runs from the lower right to the upper left.** The bridge is a low trestle footbridge crossing the river diagonally. Its right-hand end comes down onto the sandy/rocky bank on the right of the picture, exactly at the spot where a woman in an orange conical sedge hat is standing at the bridge head. From there the deck rises gently leftwards, crosses a slight apex over the mid-river trestle, and then continues to the pale sandy shore on the left bank. So the bridge has only two ends: a right-hand (near) end and a left-hand (far) end.

**2. All three figures are drawn facing left.** In each of the three figures the pale oval of the face is on the *left* side of the head and the black mass of hair is behind it on the *right* side:
- The man in the striped kimono has his face in profile on the left, his topknot behind on the right, and his body inclined forward to the left in a walking stride.
- The woman in white has her face on the left and her dressed hair, with a hairpin, behind her on the right; her kimono collar opens toward the left while the red bundle and the umbrella trail behind her on the right.
- The child's small white face is likewise on the left with dark hair behind to the right, and the body leans left.

Since they are walking forwards — that is, in the direction they are facing — they are moving **leftwards** along the bridge.

**3. Walking leftwards means they entered the bridge at its right-hand end.** Their direction of travel is toward the left bank, so the bank behind them, the one they stepped onto the bridge from, is the right-hand one.

**4. The order of the group supports this.** The party is strung out along the bridge with the child furthest ahead (leftmost), the man next, and the woman last and nearest the right-hand end. The rearmost member of a walking party is the one closest to the point of entry, which is again the right-hand end of the bridge.

**5. The surrounding traffic supports it too.** On the right-hand bank, at the very foot of the bridge, a woman in an orange sedge hat stands as if about to step onto the bridge, and a second traveller with a red bundle walks the path behind her beneath the red torii gate. That right-hand bank is clearly the approach side, served by the cliff path and the shrine gate, from which people set out across the water.

## In other words

If the three figures on the bridge are walking forwards, they have come from the right-hand (torii-gate) bank of the river and are crossing toward the left-hand bank.
